observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with white walls, a dark ceiling holding track spotlights, a light wood floor, and a full-height mirror wall on the right. A woman with a ponytail and braids, wearing a gray tank top, a yellow skirt with a yellow jacket tied at the waist, yellow leg warmers and white shoes, stands center-left of frame facing the mirror. Her mirror reflection (front view) appears center-right; it is a reflection, not a second person. The camera remains fixed throughout; background elements (AC unit, ceiling lights, curtain, wall braces) do not shift, so all apparent motion is the dancer's own movement.
visible_changes: t=0.00-0.08: dancer stands nearly still with arms held slightly out to the sides, body angled toward the mirror; only micro-adjustments of posture and arm position occur.
t=0.12-0.24: she initiates a step/lift, raising one foot off the floor and bending the knee while the arms stay partly extended; the reflection shows the matching leg lift.
t=0.28-0.44: she continues a stepping motion, drawing one leg up and forward and bringing both hands up in front of the chest/face with palms inward.
t=0.48-0.64: she holds a bent-knee pose with one foot pointed/extended to the side and hands raised near the upper chest, then begins to lower the arms.
t=0.68-0.88: she sinks into a wider squat, feet apart, hands dropping toward the thighs/knees; the yellow skirt flares outward as the hips lower.
t=0.92-1.20: she stays in the low wide stance, extending both arms forward/outward at waist height with a small sway; the skirt keeps moving with the body.
t=1.24-1.40: she rises from the squat, shifts weight and turns the torso, swinging the arms down and back as the legs straighten.
t=1.44-1.60: she raises both arms in front at shoulder/head height with palms facing forward (a push/stop-like gesture), one leg trailing behind; the clip ends mid-pose with the gesture still held.
outside_clip_unknowns: The choreography before t=0 and after t=1.6 is not shown; this is a continuous dance phrase cropped at both ends, so the routine's start and finish are unseen.
Whether the segment is practice, performance, or instruction, and any accompanying music or cues, cannot be determined from the frames.
uncertain_details: The exact identity of which leg is the support vs. moving leg is hard to fix because the dancer faces partly away and the view is mirrored; only the relative limb motion (lift, extension, squat, rise) is reliably observed.
Small arm/hand repositionings between adjacent frames are subtle and could be brief transitions rather than held poses.
No camera pan or zoom is evident, but minor framing differences cannot be fully excluded given the static background.
